The gap store now serves 1586 gap(s). Within the last 14 days it served 9275 (recorded 2026-09-18T16:27:40.184Z), so it has lost roughly 83% of its rows.

THIS IS NOT ATTRITION. Closing a gap does not remove its row — closed gaps persist with status "closed" — so this series is expected to be monotonic apart from deliberate pruning. A drop of this size means rows that existed are no longer being served.

PRECEDENT (2026-09-09): the store served 4,113 gaps at 14:35 and 44 at 22:59 across a development-vessel restart, and nothing reported it. The write path is correct atomic practice — unique per-writer tmp, in-process read-modify-write lock, then rename — so the likely mechanism is not a torn rename but a PARTIAL LOAD followed by a save, which atomically replaces a good file with a small one. Recovery that day came from orphaned atomic-write temps (gaps.json.<pid>.<n>.tmp) that had never been renamed, plus a pre-merge backup.

FIRST DIAGNOSTIC STEPS, in order: (1) do NOT write to the store until this is resolved — a save now will make the small state canonical; (2) read WORKSPACE_ROOT from the VESSEL process (/proc/<MainPID>/environ), because several stale gaps.json copies exist on the box and one carries a fresh mtime over months-old records; (3) look for unrenamed .tmp siblings of the live gaps.json, newest parseable first; (4) re-read the store immediately before any repair write — a store mid-recovery is indistinguishable from one that lost data, and a merge computed against the wrong snapshot restores nothing.

CONSEQUENCE FOR LAW 7: the gap triple (close rate, latency, durability) is computed over this store. Any closure statistic spanning the loss window is measuring a store that changed size underneath it.

Dispatches 4e0f78b6, d5f89ee9 and 0ba7b4c2 (2026-09-20 03:33Z) each returned reached:yes with reach tags 'reached:true, completion_shapes:shellResult,memoryNote_write'. Each goal named a memoryNote title and a deterministic product, which is exactly the family goal-host's transform-oracle (index.ts:3575) handles: it parses the operands, computes the expected value, reads the note back and requires nb.trim() === dtExpected, with a settle-confirm re-read. Every one of those notes stored an enveloped body that cannot equal the expected digits, so the oracle's verdict must be false, yet reach was granted anyway. Reach is therefore being decided by shape presence rather than by the artifact oracle that exists for this exact case.

summary: The uiQuestion read handler in repos/human-surface-vessel/src/routes/impulses.ts returns only panels whose kind is exactly 'question', so panels written with kind 'gap_needs_human' (the substrate's primary autonomous escalation, fired by gap_to_feature at 8+ failed repairs) never appear in the question list or the /api/questions browser route. The predecessor vessel's filter deliberately includes gap_needs_human after this exact omission previously missed every real escalation. Required behavior: a panel representing a request for human participation must be listed by the uiQuestion read regardless of which escalation kind produced it.

The participation journal writer in repos/human-surface-vessel/src/store.ts appends flat camelCase Feedback entries ({panelId, panelRevision, kind, value, ...}) to interactor-log/uiFeedback_write.jsonl, but every existing consumer of that file parses records as {pointer:{panel_id, kind}} (snake_case under a pointer wrapper). Empirically confirmed: running the consumer's exact extraction logic over a journal line produced by recordFeedback yields an empty answered-panel set, so every human answer stored by this vessel is invisible to solicitation outcome scanning and escalation disposition. Required behavior: a record appended by the participation journal must be extractable by the established interactor-log record format, or the divergence must be resolved deliberately on both sides.

REOPENED after substrate-authored 175b9f1: the patch routes through resolveObsidianEndpointViaDiscovery, which resolves discovery pointer {type: vesselCapability, shape: 'obsidian:note'} — the obsidian vessel, not the producer of uiQuestion. When an obsidian vessel is registered, uiQuestion resolves are now sent to a vessel that does not serve that shape, the fetch fails into the silent catch, ids stays empty, and the scan is a guaranteed no-op again — the exact prior failure the resolver's own comment at src/resolvers/solicitation-outcome-scan.ts:31-35 records. The one missing fact: the discovery query must name the shape the caller consumes — pointer {type: 'vesselCapability', shape: 'uiQuestion'} — and use the returned vessel's endpoint. The existing helper cannot be reused as-is because its shape is hardcoded; either add a shape parameter or a sibling resolveShapeEndpointViaDiscovery('uiQuestion'). Required behavior unchanged: resolve the uiQuestion producer through discovery by shape, with the env var and 8270 as fallbacks.

Observation, root cause not yet localized — investigate before editing anything. The stateful-ui vessel has been healthy for 21+ hours (health endpoint ok, 434 panels) yet its discovery heartbeat receives 404 'Vessel not found - must register first', while a registry shapes/vessels query still lists it as the producer of uiQuestion. During the same period the walk resolved every ui read shape (uiQuestion, uiFeedback, human_input) only through satisfier fallbacks, consistent with routing never reaching the healthy vessel. Two authorities about one registration disagree; the required behavior is that a vessel whose heartbeat is rejected re-registers (or the registry answers heartbeat and query from the same record), and that a shape listed in the registry is actually reachable by the walk.

The trend-expectation checker derives its violation gap id as 'gap-trend-expectation-violated-' + family, but multiple standing commitments can share a family. Live instance 2026-09-20: the note expectation-trend:deterministic-battery carries family=product (backfilled), and the self-minted note expectation-trend:product has the same family. The battery is in deep regression (history 3/3 -> 2/3 -> 1/3 -> 0/3 at 06:52, violated=true) while the product note scores 3/3 - and BOTH write gap-trend-expectation-violated-product. The product note's recovery closes the violation the battery filed, so a real regression's demand signal is erased by an unrelated commitment's health. Journal shows the resulting churn: event-driven pickups for gap-trend-expectation-violated-product '(reopened)' at 06:04 within the same second. This is a counterfeit-closure channel inside the honesty mechanism itself.
evidence: development-vessel/src/index.ts trend block: const gapId = 'gap-trend-expectation-violated-' + famKey; note histories: deterministic-battery last_score 0/3 open_violation true, product last_score 3/3 open_violation false; journalctl 06:04:26 shows pickup 'triggered by gap-trend-expectation-violated-product (reopened)' twice in one second
proposed_fix: Key the violation gap by the COMMITMENT, not the family: gapId = 'gap-trend-expectation-violated-' + slug(note title). Each standing bar then owns its violation lifecycle; recovery of one commitment can only close its own gap. Falsifier: with the battery below bar and the product note at 3/3, the store must contain an OPEN violation gap for the battery note and a CLOSED one for product, simultaneously.
